newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen bourse mulls new financial instruments.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen bourse mulls new financial instruments.

text.p: The Shenzhen stock exchange will launch several financial instruments on a trial basis in a bid to strengthen its market position, the Futures Herald said on Monday.
Among the instruments to be considered were covered warrants and convertible bonds, the newspaper quoted exchange president Zhuang Xinyi as saying.
He gave no timetable for the introduction of the new products.
The exchange official also said that Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, might allow the free convertibility of the Chinese currency against the Hong Kong dollar on an experimental basis.

This could be done before the renminbi is made convertible nationwide, he said without giving any official source for his belief. He said this would help to attract new investment from Hong Kong into Shenzhen's A share market, which is now reserved for domestic investors.
China has said it wants to make the renminbi convertible on the current account before the end of this year.

The newspaper also said that the south China exchange would try to introduce a market maker system for its B share and spot treasury bond trading. This would add to liquidity and reduce volatility, it said.
Shenzhen B shares, traded in Hong Kong dollars, are designed for foreign investors but domestic traders with access to foreign currency have been active in the market.
The research unit of the exchange had previously issued a report which suggested the introduction of the new financial instruments on an experimental basis, the newspaper said.
